validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real, FERC-certificated project. Docket CP15-17-000/PF14-1-000: Sabal Trail Transmission, LLC filed its NGA sec.7(c) application Nov 21, 2014 (govinfo FR-2014-12-11/2014-29049, 'requesting authorization to construct, own, and operate a new 500-mile natural gas pipeline system (Sabal Trail Project) ... in Alabama, Georgia, and Florida'), independently corroborated by a contemporaneous Dec 19, 2014 WWALS Watershed Coalition article referencing 'Sabal Trail's formal filing of 21 November 2014 in docket CP15-17'. Certificated by FERC's Feb 2, 2016 order (154 FERC P61,080, per the 2021 extension notice) and confirmed by PRNewswire's Feb 3, 2016 'Sabal Trail Transmission Project Receives FERC Certificate' release. The mainline (Phases I-II) has been operating since 2017 and is swept in a prior batch; THIS row is specifically Phase III, the remaining authorized-but-uncompleted scope: installation of two compressor units at two already-existing compressor stations (govinfo FR-2025-04-08/2025-06019: 'The remaining construction ... Phase III of the Project, involves the installation of two compressor units, one each at two existing compressor stations'). Phase III genuinely exists as an open, active FERC matter -- most recently a May 2025 extension-of-time request/grant (docket accession 20260824-5071 referenced in a WWALS Aug 25 2026 article, confirming 'nothing else has been filed in it since May 2025' beyond that extension). CLASSIFICATION: correct -- interstate natural gas transmission pipeline, not gathering/feeder (Enbridge's own factsheet: 'an interstate natural gas pipeline project'; sabaltrailtransmission.com: 'a 517-mile interstate natural gas pipeline'). DUPLICATE: not a duplicate of any of the other 43 rows in this roster; per the orchestrator's own family note this is a singleton on a system already swept in slice 1 ('P2605 Sabal Trail Phase III (Phases I-II swept)'). IMPORTANT DISCOVERY LEAD, NOT CONFLATED WITH THIS ROW: a WWALS Watershed Coalition article dated 2026-08-25 describes a genuinely NEW, separate 'Sabal Trail Expansion Project' -- a proposed second/parallel pipeline that would roughly double capacity, reportedly to serve hyperscale AI datacenter demand, first reported by WWALS in an 2026-08-14 article ('Sabal Trail wants a second pipeline and bigger compressor stations'). This new project has NO GEM ProjectID yet and is entirely distinct from Phase III (the 'two compressor units at existing stations' scope this row P2605 tracks); it is not staged as a cross_row_leads entry because that field requires an existing roster PID, and none exists for it. Flagging here so a researcher considers it for Discovery, and so it is never mistaken for P2605's own scope. ATTRIBUTION: Owner1=Sabal Trail Transmission LLC (100%) and Operator=Enbridge both corroborated -- see the Owner/Operator fills. LOCATION CAVEAT (aggregate-vs-segment): the recorded StartState/Province=Alabama, EndState/Province=Florida correctly describe the overall Sabal Trail SYSTEM's termini (govinfo 2014-29049: 'in Alabama, Georgia, and Florida'; NGI: interconnect in Tallapoosa County, AL to an interconnect near Intercession City, FL) -- but Phase III's OWN two compressor units are specifically sited in Dougherty County, GEORGIA and Suwannee County, FLORIDA (govinfo 2025-06019), not Alabama. This is not a factual error in the Location cell (the system-level corridor framing matches how the sibling Hillabee Phase 3 row in this same batch records its own phase's state), but it is worth a researcher's awareness that Phase III's physical facilities themselves are GA/FL only. Not filing this as a hard concern since it does not misstate a fact, only a level of aggregation; noted here as a caveat per the standing aggregate-vs-segment rule.

validity.researcher_notes: The recorded 76.00 MMcf/d (76,000 Dth/d) for Phase III specifically could not be directly, precisely corroborated. An S&P Global Platts article ('Sabal Trail seeks two-year extension on construction deadline for compressors') that WebSearch snippets indicate states a '76,000 Dt/d' figure for Phase III would be an exact match, but every fetch attempt on spglobal.com (3 different article URLs) returned HTTP 403 to both WebFetch and curl with a realistic browser User-Agent, and the Wayback Machine capture could not be checked either -- archive.org's CDX API returned HTTP 429 (rate-limited) on every retry across this session, including after waiting. I derived an approximate corroboration instead: NaturalGasIntel's original 2015 FERC-approval article states the whole Sabal Trail system would 'provide up to 1.07 million Dth/d of firm service' (the total mainline target, i.e. Phases I+II+III combined), while FERC's April 2025 extension notice (govinfo 2025-06019) states the first two phases already built comprise '999,000 dekatherms per day (Dth/d) of capacity.' The residual, 1,070,000 - 999,000 = ~71,000 Dth/d, is in the same order of magnitude as the recorded 76,000 Dth/d but not an exact match (~7% gap) -- NGI's 'up to 1.07 million' is itself a rounded 2015-era ceiling figure, so the true residual could plausibly be closer to 76,000. Staging this as the fill's REFS_ADDED support at medium tier (see the Capacity fill) since it is corroborative, not contradictory, but filing this concern so a researcher with access to the blocked S&P Global article (or the underlying FERC certificate's Phase III capacity table) can confirm the exact 76,000 Dth/d figure directly rather than relying on my derived residual.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Sheet's LastUpdated is 2025-09-22. A WWALS Watershed Coalition article dated 2026-08-25 -- genuinely newer than the sheet's LastUpdated -- independently confirms via FERC docket monitoring that this extension was GRANTED and that 'nothing else has been filed in [docket CP15-17] since May 2025,' i.e., Phase III still has not been completed or placed into service as of Aug 2026. This is NOT a dormancy/staleness case: there IS recent, dated, affirmative evidence (a live 2025 regulatory filing independently reported in Aug 2026), it simply confirms the project remains in the same not-yet-built state the sheet already records. I also checked whether Phase III might actually be under active construction (which would argue for verdict=change to 'construction') -- no source found describes construction activity underway; the WWALS article's own framing treats the docket as essentially dormant aside from the extension paperwork. I also checked for whether the FERC certificate holder might have abandoned/withdrawn Phase III (which would argue for shelved/cancelled) -- no such filing or announcement was found; on the contrary, an actively-requested-and-granted extension of time is evidence the sponsor still intends to complete it, which argues against inferring dormancy under the 2y->shelved rule even though the physical work itself has been delayed for years. Recommend Status remain 'proposed' (verdict=confirm). Separately noted (see validity, discovery lead): WWALS also reports on a genuinely NEW, second 'Sabal Trail Expansion Project' (a proposed additional/parallel pipeline) that has no GEM PID -- not conflated with this row's Phase III status.
